title: Prawn Bisque
subtitle: Classic French shellfish cream soup
excerpt: The great French shellfish soup: prawn shells roasted in butter with brandy, then simmered with aromatics and cream into a deep orange bisque of extraordinary richness and depth. The shells are where the flavour lives.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bisque is a rich, creamy French shellfish soup with origins in the coastal regions of France. The defining technique is the use of the shells: the crab, lobster, or prawn shells are roasted until very hot, then flambéed with cognac, and simmered at length with aromatics to extract every trace of flavour. The soup is finished with cream and often with a little rice or flour to thicken it. The word bisque may derive from the Bay of Biscay (Biscaye in French) or from the old French 'bis cuites' (twice-cooked). A prawn bisque is the most accessible home version: bought shell-on prawns provide the shells and the cooked prawn meat becomes the garnish.

content.text: Do not skip the step of frying the shells until they are very fragrant and have coloured the butter orange; this is where the bisque gets its characteristic deep flavour. Blend the soup in a powerful blender with the shells for maximum extraction, then strain very thoroughly through a fine sieve. The shell material left behind contains no more flavour by this point.

items.preparation: shell-on; peel and reserve the shells; devein the meat

content.text: Fry the prawn shells in the butter over very high heat, pressing them down, for 3 to 4 minutes until they turn orange and fragrant. Add the brandy and cook for 30 seconds. Add the vegetables, garlic, tomatoes, tomato puree, bay, and thyme. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the stock. Simmer for 25 minutes. Blend the whole mixture thoroughly, including the shells. Pass through a very fine sieve or muslin, pressing hard to extract all the liquid.

Return the strained bisque to the pan. Add the cream. Season with salt and cayenne. Cook the reserved prawn meat in a little butter for 2 minutes until just pink. Serve the bisque in warm bowls with the prawns on top.
